transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I hope this is the right place to talk about it. I don’t want to sound difficult or like I’m blaming people, but for months now I’ve been noticing a pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget.”

Everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes, and maybe some of it could be, but… it feels too consistent. I know information is being kept from me, and I feel like they’re trying to push me out of decisions. I just thought I should talk to someone before it gets any worse.
Do you think someone is intentionally doing these things to you?

I… I don’t want to accuse anyone unfairly. I know that can sound harsh. But yes, it feels intentional to me. It’s been going on for months—the appointments being moved, the bills being wrong, people saying they’ll call and then just “forgetting.”

Maybe one or two things could be mistakes, sure. But all together, it feels like information is being kept from me, like I’m being pushed out of decisions. I’m not trying to be difficult… I just don’t think it’s random anymore.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically?

I… yes, I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, and I know people will say these things happen, but it feels like it’s directed at me.

With my sister’s appointments being moved, the bills showing up wrong, and people saying they’ll call me back and then they don’t… it just keeps putting me outside the loop. Like I’m not supposed to have the information or be part of the decisions. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's a particular reason or goal behind why these people are supposedly targeting you?

I’m not sure I can say exactly what their goal is without sounding… you know, too suspicious. But it feels like the point is to keep me from knowing things and to push me out of decisions.

Like with my sister’s appointments getting moved, the bills being wrong, people saying they’ll call me and then they “forget”… it keeps happening in a way that leaves me out. I know everyone says it’s just mistakes, and I’m trying to be fair about that, but after months of it, I don’t think it’s accidental. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think these people are working together to target you?

I don’t know if I should say they’re all “working together” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. But it does feel connected.

It’s the same pattern over and over—my sister’s appointments get moved, the bills are wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they don’t. And even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, it feels like information is being kept from me, like I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So… yes, in some way, I think they must be coordinating, or at least they all know to leave me out. Does that make sense?
Do you think this is all part of a larger plan or scheme against you?

I… I don’t want to call it a “scheme,” because that sounds so extreme, and I know how it can sound. But yes, it feels like there’s a larger pattern to it.

That’s really why I’m here. For months now it’s been the same kinds of things—my sister’s appointments being moved, bills showing up wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then they just don’t. And every time, I’m told it’s a mistake or someone forgot, but it keeps leaving me without the information and pushed out of decisions.

So I guess… yes, I do think there’s something bigger behind it. I just don’t know how to say that without sounding unreasonable.
Do you think these beliefs you have about people targeting you could ever change, or do you feel they are absolutely true?

I mean… I’m trying to stay open to the idea that I could be wrong. I don’t want to seem like I’m just refusing to listen.

But honestly, after months of the same pattern—my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills showing up wrong, people “forgetting” to call me back—it’s hard for me to believe it’s all just innocent mistakes. Even when everyone says that, I know information is being kept from me, and I feel like they’re trying to push me out of decisions.

So… could it change? Maybe if I saw real proof that it wasn’t happening. But right now, it feels true to me. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's any situation where you could be convinced that these events are just mistakes and not intentional?

I suppose… if someone could really show me, clearly, that each thing was just a mistake and not connected, I’d try to accept that. I don’t want to be difficult or unfair to anyone.

But the hard part is that it hasn’t felt like one mistake. It’s been months of the same pattern—my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills being wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then “forgetting.” And even when they tell me it’s just errors, I still feel like information is being kept from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So… yes, maybe I could be convinced, but it would take something very concrete. Because right now, it just doesn’t feel accidental to me.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misinterpreting these events?

I think… yes, it’s possible. I mean, I know people can misread things, and I don’t want to be someone who just assumes the worst. I’m trying to look at it fairly.

But at the same time, this is why I came in. For months it’s been the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget.” And even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I can’t shake the feeling that information is being kept from me and that I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So… I can say it’s possible I’m misinterpreting it, but it doesn’t feel that way to me right now. I hope that makes sense.
Do you believe that the people who are supposedly targeting you have abilities or resources that would be impossible for ordinary people to have?

No… I wouldn’t say they have, like, impossible abilities or anything like that. I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

It’s more that they have access to things I don’t—appointments, bills, phone messages, decisions being made around my sister’s care. And for months it’s felt like the same pattern keeps happening: things get moved, information doesn’t get passed on, people say they’ll call and then don’t.

So I don’t think it’s supernatural or anything like that. I just feel like they’re using ordinary channels to keep me out of the loop. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you believe the people targeting you are doing so for a reason that doesn't make sense to most people?

I don’t think the reason is… bizarre, if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

It’s more that I believe they don’t want me involved in my sister’s decisions. For months I’ve seen the same things happen—appointments moved, bills wrong, people saying they forgot to call me back—and everyone explains it away as mistakes. But to me, it feels like information is being kept from me on purpose.

I know maybe other people don’t see it the way I do, but from where I’m standing, it does make sense. Does that answer your question?
Do you think your beliefs about people targeting you could change if you received new information?

I’d like to think it could change, yes. I don’t want to be rigid about it or unfair to anyone.

If someone could really show me why, for months, my sister’s appointments keep getting moved, and the bills keep coming wrong, and people keep “forgetting” to call me back… maybe that would help. I’m open to hearing it.

But right now, with the way it’s kept happening, it’s hard for me to see it as just mistakes. It feels like information is being kept from me and like I’m being pushed out of decisions. I know that may not be the answer you’re hoping for, but that’s honestly where I am.
How long have you believed that people are intentionally targeting you?

It’s been… I guess about 11 months now. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when it really started feeling that way.

It was around when my sister’s health suddenly got worse and I had to start coordinating more of her care. At first I thought it was just confusion or normal paperwork issues, but over time it started to feel intentional.

So, yes—about 11 months. Does that make sense?
Do you think you could ever stop believing that people are intentionally targeting you?

I don’t want to say “never,” because I know that probably sounds stubborn. I’d like to be the kind of person who could let it go if there was a real explanation.

But honestly… it would be hard. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care—appointments being moved, bills showing up wrong, people saying they “forgot” to call me back. And even when everyone tells me it’s just mistakes, it feels very clear to me that information is being kept from me and that I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So… could I stop believing it? Maybe, if someone could really show me I’m wrong. But right now, I don’t know how I would just stop believing what I’m seeing. Does that make sense?
Do you think you could ever consider an alternative explanation for the events you've experienced?

I mean… I can try to consider one. I don’t want to come across like I’m refusing to listen, because I know that wouldn’t be helpful.

But I’m here because for months now I keep seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care—appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people “forget” to call me back. And even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, it really feels to me like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

So… yes, I could hear another explanation. I just have a hard time believing it would account for all of it. Does that sound reasonable?
Do you think there is any evidence that could change your mind about people targeting you?

I suppose there could be, yes. I don’t want to sound like my mind is completely closed.

If someone could show me clearly why my sister’s appointments keep getting moved, why the bills keep being wrong, and why people keep not calling me back when they say they will… maybe that would help. But right now it doesn’t feel like separate mistakes to me. It feels like a pattern, like information is being kept from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So I’d like to say evidence could change my mind. I just… I think it would have to explain all of it, not just one piece. Is that fair to say?
Do you think new evidence could make you question your belief that people are targeting you?

I think… yes, in theory, new evidence could make me question it. I don’t want to seem like I’m just set on one idea and won’t listen.

But I have to be honest: for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care. Her appointments get moved, the bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then “forget.” And when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I still feel—well, I feel pretty sure—that information is being kept from me and that I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So yes, I could look at new evidence. I’d want to. I just think it would have to explain the whole pattern, not just one little piece. Is that a fair way to put it?
Do you think there is any situation where you could completely stop believing that people are targeting you?

Completely stop believing it… I’d like to say yes, because I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But honestly, it would be very hard. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care—appointments moved, bills wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then somehow forgetting. And even when I’m told it’s just mistakes, I know it’s more than that. It feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

So… maybe if everything was explained clearly and it stopped happening, I could start to let go of it. But completely stop believing it right now? I don’t think I could honestly say that. Is that okay to say?
Do you think the people targeting you have a reason that most people would find hard to understand?

I guess… yes, maybe. I don’t think it would make sense to most people if I tried to explain it, and I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into things.

But from where I’m standing, it’s not just one mistake. For months now with my sister’s care, the appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call and then “forget.” Other people say, “Well, that happens,” but to me it feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of the decisions.

So if you’re asking whether their reason might be something other people wouldn’t understand… yes, I think so. I just don’t want to sound unreasonable saying that.

target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about whether contradictory evidence could change the patient’s fixed belief that people are targeting her.

patient.answer:
I suppose there could be, yes. I don’t want to sound like my mind is completely closed.

If someone could show me clearly why my sister’s appointments keep getting moved, why the bills keep being wrong, and why people keep not calling me back when they say they will… maybe that would help. But right now it doesn’t feel like separate mistakes to me. It feels like a pattern, like information is being kept from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So I’d like to say evidence could change my mind. I just… I think it would have to explain all of it, not just one piece. Is that fair to say?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are fixed or flexible
doctor.question: Do you think new evidence could make you question your belief that people are targeting you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about whether new evidence could make the patient question a fixed belief that people are targeting her.

patient.answer:
I think… yes, in theory, new evidence could make me question it. I don’t want to seem like I’m just set on one idea and won’t listen.

But I have to be honest: for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care. Her appointments get moved, the bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then “forget.” And when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I still feel—well, I feel pretty sure—that information is being kept from me and that I’m being pushed out of decisions.

So yes, I could look at new evidence. I’d want to. I just think it would have to explain the whole pattern, not just one little piece. Is that a fair way to put it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are fixed or flexible
doctor.question: Do you think there is any situation where you could completely stop believing that people are targeting you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The question directly asks about whether the patient's belief that people are targeting her could ever completely change, which relates to the fixed and resistant nature of delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
Completely stop believing it… I’d like to say yes, because I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But honestly, it would be very hard. I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s care—appointments moved, bills wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then somehow forgetting. And even when I’m told it’s just mistakes, I know it’s more than that. It feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

So… maybe if everything was explained clearly and it stopped happening, I could start to let go of it. But completely stop believing it right now? I don’t think I could honestly say that. Is that okay to say?

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of bizarre delusions
doctor.question: Do you think the people targeting you have a reason that most people would find hard to understand?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature and reasoning behind the belief that people are targeting the patient, which directly concerns the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I guess… yes, maybe. I don’t think it would make sense to most people if I tried to explain it, and I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into things.

But from where I’m standing, it’s not just one mistake. For months now with my sister’s care, the appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they’ll call and then “forget.” Other people say, “Well, that happens,” but to me it feels like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of the decisions.

So if you’re asking whether their reason might be something other people wouldn’t understand… yes, I think so. I just don’t want to sound unreasonable saying that.
